slot.brief: Given a structure described in text (e.g. a substituted cycloalkene or a chain with halogen and OH), pick its correct IUPAC name — standard nomenclature with one correct and three near-miss options.

stem: The IUPAC name of the compound CH2=C(CH3)-CHBr-CH2OH is:

verdicts.working: Number from the OH end: the parent is but-3-en-1-ol, with bromo at C2 and methyl at C3.

working:
Principal functional group is OH, so suffix is -ol. Number the longest chain from the OH end: C1=OH, C2=Br, C3=methyl, C4=CH2, with double bond between C3 and C4. Name: 2-bromo-3-methylbut-3-en-1-ol.

Independent check: Number from the OH end: the parent is but-3-en-1-ol, with bromo at C2 and methyl at C3.
solution: The $-OH$ group gets the lowest locant, so number the chain from the $CH_2OH$ end. The parent chain is but-3-en-1-ol, with bromo at C2 and methyl at C3: $\boxed{2\text{-bromo-}3\text{-methylbut-3-en-1-ol}}$.
